$comment: templates/ci-lanes.json -- the CI workflow `nen scaffold init` writes when the declaration has MORE THAN ONE lane -- several stacks, or one stack in several directories (zheref/nen#586). A per-stack template's `ci` body runs every verb against the declaration's default lane, and a multi-lane declaration has none, so this one file is the header once plus `job` once per lane, in lane order. `{{job}}` is `shu-` plus the lane name with `.` replaced by `_` (job ids take no dot, and ignore case, so two lanes that would collide are refused); `{{lane}}` is the lane name single-quoted for YAML; `{{runner}}` is the runner that lane's own stack template names. A lane whose stack has no template (the pack's `scaffoldTemplate` is null), or whose name is not a plain token, gets no job -- and then NO workflow is written at all, with the manual step named, because a workflow that silently skips a lane is the defect this file exists to end. It sits beside index.json rather than in a directory because it is not a template a stack is pointed at: it serves every stack that has one.
header:
# .github/workflows/nen-shu.yml -- written by `nen scaffold`, one job per lane.
#
# This repository declares more than one lane, so no lane is the default:
# each lane is its own job on its own stack's runner, and every verb names
# its lane with `--lane`.
# Every argv those verbs run comes from THIS repository's own
# nen/contract.json. Nothing in this file names a build tool, a package
# manager or a test runner, and nothing in it should: to change what CI runs,
# change the declaration. A lane added to the declaration later is NOT added
# here -- copy a job below and change its lane.
name: nen shu

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# READ-ONLY BY DECLARATION. This workflow fetches a pinned nen release over
# plain HTTPS and runs `nen shu` verbs against the checkout; it pushes nothing,
# comments on nothing and opens nothing.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
job:
{{job}}:
    runs-on: {{runner}}
    env:
      NEN_LANE: {{lane}}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Pinned by ref. Re-pinning this repository is this one value in every
      # job; the bootstrap verifies the binary it fetches against the release
      # manifest.
      - name: nen
        env:
          NEN_REF: {{nenRef}}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zheref/nen/${NEN_REF}/bootstrap/nen.sh" -o nen-bootstrap.sh
          echo "NEN=$(bash nen-bootstrap.sh --ref "${NEN_REF}")" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

      # Read-only: what this runner has against what the lane pins. Exit 5 is
      # "a pinned tool is missing" and fails the job; exit 7 is "nen is behind
      # dependency.pinned_ref" -- drift in this file -- and is a warning.
      - name: toolchain
        run: |
          set +e
          "${NEN}" shu tools --repo . --lane "${NEN_LANE}"
          status=$?
          if [ "${status}" -eq 7 ]; then
            echo "::warning title=nen behind pinned_ref::NEN_REF in this workflow is older than dependency.pinned_ref in nen/contract.json -- repin this file's NEN_REF."
            exit 0
          fi
          exit "${status}"

      # --dry-run FIRST on every verb, so a declaration that drifted fails here
      # rather than half-way through a real build.
      - name: build / test / lint
        run: |
          set +e
          for verb in build test lint; do
            # The empty second form is deliberately unquoted: it must vanish.
            for form in "--dry-run" ""; do
              "${NEN}" shu "${verb}" --repo . --lane "${NEN_LANE}" ${form}
              status=$?
              [ "${status}" -eq 0 ] && continue
              # 4 is "this lane declares no such verb" -- a fact about the
              # repository, not a failure of the run.
              [ "${status}" -eq 4 ] && { echo "shu ${verb}: not declared for lane ${NEN_LANE}"; break; }
              exit "${status}"
            done
          done
